brief: The canvas displays a cross-section of a massive canyon revealing the slow, persistent history of a riverbank. The scene is composed entirely of dense, layered concrete material, rendered in muted, earthy tones. The viewer observes distinct, horizontal stripes representing accumulated sediment, showcasing the effects of deep time and continuous geological processes. Nothing on the canvas changes when the viewer interacts with it; instead, the entire composition exhibits a slow, inevitable evolution, subtly building up new layers and redefining the visible strata as if viewed through a geological time-lapse.

statement: This sketch presents a monumental bronze heart structure rendered in a volumetric cross-section, evoking the slow, continuous processes of geological formation. The composition builds upon the concept of deep time through layered material accumulation, but transforms it into an organic, pulsing biological form. The heart's walls are composed of horizontal strata that subtly shift and pulse with time, suggesting the rhythmic beating of a city-sized organ. Through constant, imperceptible motion, the layers build up and redefine themselves, creating a sense of perpetual evolution and growth within a single moment. The muted bronze tones and volumetric rendering create an atmosphere of ancient durability and organic vitality simultaneously.
